binders: A fixed probability space (Ω,Σ,P) [PDF page 1; printed page 5, final paragraph].
Real-valued random variables X,Y∈L2(Ω,Σ,P) [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1; PDF page 2; printed page 6, opening display and Equation (1.1)].
hypotheses: (Ω,Σ,P) is a probability space; the source imposes no additional conditions such as atomlessness, independence, centering, or identical distribution [PDF pages 1–2; printed pages 5–6, surrounding Section 1.1 context].
X and Y have finite L2 norm, equivalently finite second absolute moment E|X|^2<∞ and E|Y|^2<∞ [PDF page 1; printed page 5, Lp-norm definition; PDF page 2; printed page 6, definition of Lp].
conclusions: L2 is a Hilbert space [PDF page 2; printed page 6, paragraph immediately preceding Equation (1.1)].
For X,Y∈L2, ⟨X,Y⟩_{L2}=E(XY) [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1), first identity].
For X∈L2, ||X||_{L2}=(E|X|^2)^{1/2} [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1), second identity].
definitions_and_conventions: For p∈(0,∞), ||X||_{Lp}:=(E|X|^p)^{1/p} [PDF page 1; printed page 5, displayed Lp-norm definition].
Lp(Ω,Σ,P) consists of the random variables on Ω whose Lp norm is finite [PDF page 2; printed page 6, opening display].
Expectation E X is the Lebesgue integral of the real-valued function X:Ω→R [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1].
Expectation brackets are suppressed: E f(X) means E[f(X)], and function application binds before expectation [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 2].
The phrase “corresponding norm” identifies the second formula as the norm induced by the first inner product [PDF page 2; printed page 6, sentence introducing Equation (1.1)].
implicit_context: “Random variable” carries its standard measurability requirement, although measurability is not redefined in the selected passage [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1 and surrounding probability-space discussion].
Since X,Y∈L2, XY is integrable and E(XY) is finite; the source supports this later on the same page by the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Cauchy–Schwarz paragraph].

The source writes elements of L2 as random variables/functions X:Ω→R and never explicitly introduces almost-everywhere equivalence classes [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1; PDF page 2; printed page 6, opening display].

Calling ||·||_{L2} a norm and L2 a Hilbert space structurally invokes the standard identification of random variables equal almost surely, because without that identification the displayed quantity is only a seminorm on raw functions; this identification is inferred rather than stated [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Hilbert-space assertion and Equation (1.1)].

details: All objects live over one fixed probability space (Ω,Σ,P) [PDF page 1; printed page 5, final paragraph].
No independence, centering, distributional, or nondegeneracy assumption occurs in Equation (1.1) or its defining context [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1)].
The source's random variables are real-valued, written as functions X:Ω→R [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1].
X and Y play symmetric vector roles in the inner-product identity; the norm identity binds only X [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1)].
Equation (1.1) is an identity on L2, so each argument has finite second absolute moment [PDF page 2; printed page 6, opening display and Equation (1.1)].
The formula is not asserted for arbitrary random variables with an infinite second moment [PDF page 2; printed page 6, definition of Lp as finite-norm variables].
For X,Y∈L2, E(XY) is finite; the same page states |E XY|≤||X||_{L2}||Y||_{L2} [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Cauchy–Schwarz paragraph].
The explicit presentation uses random-variable representatives/functions and gives no quotient construction [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1; PDF page 2; printed page 6, opening display].

The norm and Hilbert-space claims require the conventional almost-everywhere identification if interpreted with full measure-theoretic precision; the source leaves this convention implicit [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Hilbert-space assertion].
The inner product is E(XY), not covariance and not E(|XY|) [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1), first identity].
The corresponding norm is exactly (E|X|^2)^{1/2} [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1), second identity].

undebatable_constraints: The ambient data are a fixed probability space (Ω,Σ,P) [PDF page 1; printed page 5, final paragraph].
The variables are real-valued random variables [PDF page 1; printed page 5, footnote 1].
The identities have L2, not arbitrary-random-variable, domain [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1) and the preceding definition of Lp].
Finite L2 norm means finite second absolute moment [PDF page 1; printed page 5, Lp-norm definition; PDF page 2; printed page 6, Lp membership definition].
Both parts of Equation (1.1) must be preserved: ⟨X,Y⟩_{L2}=E(XY) and ||X||_{L2}=(E|X|^2)^{1/2} [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1)].
The first formula defines the L2 inner product, while the second gives its corresponding norm [PDF page 2; printed page 6, sentence introducing Equation (1.1)].
No independence, centering, covariance, or variance hypothesis belongs to Equation (1.1) [PDF page 2; printed page 6, Equation (1.1); covariance appears separately in Equation (1.2).]

ambiguities.issue: The source does not explicitly say whether L2 elements are raw random-variable representatives or equivalence classes modulo almost-sure equality.
ambiguities.evidence: Printed page 5, footnote 1 calls X a function Ω→R, and printed page 6 says Lp consists of random variables X on Ω; neither passage mentions a quotient. The same printed page nevertheless calls ||·||_{L2} a norm and L2 a Hilbert space.
ambiguities.impact: A formal rendering may use measurable-function representatives or an almost-everywhere quotient, but raw functions make the displayed L2 quantity only a seminorm. Preserving the source's literal Hilbert-space and norm claims therefore requires almost-everywhere identification or an equivalent extensional convention, although the source does not specify its implementation.

contract_plain_english: On a fixed probability space (Ω,Σ,P), take real-valued square-integrable random variables X and Y. Equation (1.1) says that L2 is equipped with inner product ⟨X,Y⟩=E(XY), and that the norm induced by this inner product is ||X||=(E|X|^2)^{1/2}. Square-integrability supplies finite second moments and makes XY integrable. The book writes L2 elements as random variables/functions, while the almost-everywhere quotient needed for a literal normed Hilbert space is conventional but unstated [primary source, PDF pages 1–2; printed pages 5–6, Section 1.1 and Equation (1.1)].
